title: Two clarinets in a band and clarinet with saxophone
summary: Asked about two-clarinet bands, Barnes says it was done only occasionally; the clarinet should lead and a tenor saxophone could play variations.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Did you ever see a band lined up with two clarinets? One playing the lead, one playing variation?
Well we had it done a couple of times. It wasn't a regular thing?
It ain't right. But sometimes you take clarinet to it, you got three or four clarinets.

Well the reason why I ask you that is, there's an old photograph of Bolden's band, where he has Frank Lewis and Willie Warner both in the photograph, both with the clarinets. And I wondered if that was the reason, if they ever did have two clarinets in the band, one playing lead, one playing the lead.

Well I don't remember nothing about that. I don't know nothing about that. And I know plenty of musicians and music too. You see I don't say I know music, but I know some of them. You certainly know more than most people. Yeah, but in the meantime for clarinets to do that, they can put two clarinets together. But a clarinet is supposed to use a cyclic one.
He's supposed, a clarinet is supposed to use a cyc. And what I mean by cyc, he could use a tenor.
That's if there's no violin you're saying? Yeah that's right.
He could use a tenor cyc, a clarinet. He can use other cyc if you want, but his duty is to use a clarinet and a tenor cyc. That sounds funny, but it's right.
And the sax would play the variations the clarinet would lead?
